news.text: Stock fell ~6% ahead of Aug 3 earnings on valuation worries and UK NHS contract scrutiny.
Nvidia AI partnership plus Army Foundry and expanded Surf Air deals sparked a 9% rally.
D.A. Davidson upgraded to Buy; Wedbush reaffirmed $230 target on AI momentum.
Launched SoFi Small Business Loans and an AI-driven Composer investing platform this month.
Goldman raised its price target to $21 but kept a Neutral rating on the stock.
Reports Q2 earnings July 29; shares fell ~3% amid lending-practice regulatory scrutiny.
New Chairman Shawn Pelsinger took over today following the annual shareholder meeting.
Debt refinancing cut convertible notes to $16.9M and added a $30M term loan, easing liquidity.
Wheels Up signed as BrokerOS launch customer; Palantir SurfOS partnership expanded.
FY2026 earnings call is July 27 (3 days out); consensus -$0.36 EPS, $91.9M revenue.
Nvidia exited its equity stake in the company, rattling AI-datacenter valuation confidence.
Down ~50% since May on AI-capex jitters; Street stays Strong Buy, $74.50 median target.
RSI exited oversold territory July 21; MACD turned positive, historically a bullish signal.
Launched NoScrubs laundry pilot and a public-art robot program, diversifying beyond food delivery.
Q2 2026 results due August 6; stock still down roughly 50% year to date.
FDA panel backed BPC-157 peptide compounding July 23; stock popped over 10% same day.
Shares reversed hard today (-9.6%) as analysts tempered peptide enthusiasm and a CFO pre-vote stock sale drew scrutiny.
Chief Accounting Officer Irene Becklund to resign in October, staying on through transition.
Q2 beat: EPS $0.90 vs. $0.76 est., revenue +24% YoY; guidance raised.
Shares up ~4.3% today on the beat-and-raise; Now Assist AI cited as key driver.
Next earnings pushed to Oct 28 — no near-term catalyst risk remains this quarter.
Shares down ~18% YTD (29% off highs) on AI-capex spending skepticism heading into July 29 earnings.
Announced $2.5B investment in a new Microsoft Frontier AI unit; shares rose 1.6% on the news.
Analyst consensus remains Strong Buy; average target $589-592 versus a ~$384 share price.
Down ~29% YTD on AI-capex/debt concerns; FY27 capex guided toward $95B with $40B more financing planned.
FY26 results beat on record cloud growth, but shares sank on debt and cash-burn worries.
Multi-year hyperscaler AI backlog still gives strong FY27+ revenue visibility, per analysts.
Securities fraud class action filed after shares fell ~17% on Redfin anticompetitive-agreement allegations.
Jefferies cut its target to $60 (from $75); KBW cut to $37 (from $50).
Zillow Rentals launched as a connected app inside Google Gemini, expanding distribution reach.
